_what: The Den's listening bench: the songs Elvis Presley recorded in the Jungle Room at Graceland, in the order they were recorded, with the session day on each one.
_why: In 1976 the Jungle Room at Graceland was converted into a recording studio and the bulk of Presley's last two albums were made in it — From Elvis Presley Boulevard, Memphis, Tennessee (RCA, 16 May 1976) and Moody Blue (RCA, 19 July 1977). Felton Jarvis produced. The room is famous for its carpet; it is also the room those records came out of, and that is the only reason there is a subroom behind our own Jungle Room at all.
_source: 2026-09-20: the track list, the session dates, the songwriters and the album attributions were read off Wikipedia's articles on the two albums, which give a recording date per track. The video ids were NOT typed from memory and not guessed: each title was searched on YouTube, candidates were filtered to Presley's official channels, and every id that went in was then checked on its own watch page — ownerChannelName, channelId, playabilityStatus, playableInEmbed and lengthSeconds. Twelve are on 'Elvis Presley - Topic' (UChgxarBUCnPJV871-46bJ2g, the label's own art-track channel) and four on ElvisPresleyVEVO (UCSEmH1YyFWltSBYkfLMtkcg). Every runtime below was read off the watch page rather than off a search result, because the search page rounds.
_takes: MASTERS, NOT OUTTAKES. Searching any of these turns up alternate takes on the same official channels — 'Take 1', 'Take 9', a six-minute run at a three-minute song. A room built on 'these are the records that came out of that carpet' cannot quietly hand somebody a rehearsal instead. Each id here was matched against the released runtime before it went in.
_rule: The vibe, not the lyrics. Same rule as the dancefloor and the chapel: we name the artist, we name the people who WROTE it — which matters here, because Presley wrote none of these — we link the song, and we let them keep their own words. The notes are ours about the room and the session. Nothing is hosted by us.
_runtime: AND EVERY ONE OF THESE SAYS HOW LONG IT RUNS, which is the street's oldest rule and the exact rule the room upstairs cannot follow. The Jungle Room's cams never end, so make-jungle.py refuses a runtime; these are songs of a known length, so make-den.py refuses a track without one. Parent and subroom enforce opposite checks and are making the same promise: tell somebody what they are pressing before they press it.

sessions.name: February 1976
sessions.sub: The first week. Ten of these went on From Elvis Presley Boulevard, Memphis, Tennessee, out that May; two waited for Moody Blue.

tracks.title: Bitter They Are, Harder They Fall
tracks.note: The first thing cut in the room, on the first night. A Larry Gatlin song about a fall, opening a record made in a house.

tracks.title: She Thinks I Still Care
tracks.note: A George Jones standard, taken slow. Held back for a year and a half and then put on the last album.

tracks.title: The Last Farewell
tracks.writers: Roger Whittaker and Ron A. Webster
tracks.note: Four minutes, and nothing hurried in any of them. The room was a living room an hour earlier and it sounds like one.

tracks.title: Solitaire
tracks.note: Sedaka and Cody's song about a man playing cards alone, sung by a man who had stopped leaving the house to make records.

tracks.title: Moody Blue
tracks.note: The one that gave the last album its name, and the only thing in this room with a disco pulse under it. Released as a single that November.

tracks.title: I'll Never Fall in Love Again
tracks.note: Donegan's, not Bacharach and David's — two different songs with the same title, and this is the skiffle one.

tracks.title: For the Heart
tracks.note: By the man who wrote Burning Love. The band is the touring band, playing in a carpeted room with the furniture still in it.

tracks.title: Hurt
tracks.note: Two minutes and seven seconds, and the loudest thing anybody did in that room. A 1954 song he had been carrying around for twenty years.

tracks.title: Danny Boy
tracks.note: A parlour song from 1913, sung in a parlour. Of everything here this is the one that most obviously belongs in a house.

tracks.title: Never Again
tracks.writers: Billy Edd Wheeler and Jerry Chesnut
tracks.note: Short, plain, and over before it has made a fuss about itself.

tracks.title: Love Coming Down
tracks.note: The second Chesnut song of the same night, and the quieter of the two.

tracks.title: Blue Eyes Crying in the Rain
tracks.note: Fred Rose wrote it in 1945; Willie Nelson had made it a number one the year before this was cut. The last thing recorded in the February week.

sessions.name: October 1976
sessions.sub: Three nights, eight months later, in the same room. Everything from them went on Moody Blue — the album he did not live to see released.

tracks.title: Way Down
tracks.note: Released as a single on 6 June 1977 and the last one out in his lifetime. J.D. Sumner goes lower on this than anybody needed him to, which is the point of it.

tracks.title: Pledging My Love
tracks.note: Johnny Ace's 1954 record, which came out after Ace had died. Cut here in a den with a waterfall in it.

tracks.title: It's Easy for You
tracks.writers: Andrew Lloyd Webber and Tim Rice
tracks.note: Lloyd Webber and Rice, which is not a credit anybody expects to find on an Elvis record, let alone this one.

tracks.title: He'll Have to Go
tracks.note: Jim Reeves' song, taken very slow indeed. The last thing on this bench, and the last studio session of his life.
